title: The Unreliable Narrator
text:
Modern criticism has devoted considerable attention to the unreliable narrator, a figure whose account the reader cannot fully trust. In many nineteenth-century novels, the narrator appears authoritative, yet the reader gradually perceives distortions in the story being told. Such discrepancies compel the reader to reconstruct events from fragments of evidence. The technique thus transforms reading into an act of interpretation rather than passive reception.

Some scholars contend that unreliability is deliberately cultivated by authors seeking to unsettle moral certainties. Others argue that the concept is anachronistic, imposing twentieth-century suspicion upon texts written under different conventions. The debate turns on whether the reader's distrust reveals the author's design or the reader's own expectations. No consensus has emerged, and each reading tends to disclose as much about its interpreter as about the novel.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what does the reader have to do when narrative discrepancies appear?
options: Reconstruct events from fragments of evidence
Accept the narrator's account without question

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what do some scholars contend?
options: Unreliability is deliberately cultivated by authors to unsettle moral certainties
Unreliable narrators appear only in twentieth-century fiction
Readers should ignore the narrator altogether
The concept of unreliability has been fully resolved

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of reading in this passage?
options: Reading involves active interpretation rather than passive reception
Reading is pointless when a narrator is unreliable
Reading should be limited to factual texts
Readers have no role in shaping meaning

questions.text: What does the passage suggest about the debate over unreliability?
options: Interpretations may reveal as much about the reader as about the text
The debate has a clear and universally accepted answer
Only authors can decide whether a narrator is reliable
The debate concerns only the length of novels

paragraph_translations: Modern eleştiri, güvenilmez anlatıcıya, yani okurun anlatımına tam olarak güvenemeyeceği bir figüre büyük önem vermiştir. On dokuzuncu yüzyıl romanlarının birçoğunda anlatıcı otoriter görünür, ama okur zamanla anlatılan hikâyedeki çarpıtmaları fark eder. Bu tür tutarsızlıklar okuru parça parça kanıtlardan olayları yeniden kurmaya zorlar. Böylece bu teknik okumayı pasif bir alımlamadan çok bir yorumlama eylemine dönüştürür.

Bazı akademisyenler, güvenilmezliğin yazarlar tarafından ahlaki kesinlikleri sarsmak amacıyla bilinçli olarak geliştirildiğini savunur. Başkaları ise bu kavramın anakronik olduğunu, farklı kurallara göre yazılmış metinlere yirminci yüzyıl şüphesini dayattığını ileri sürer. Tartışma, okurun güvensizliğinin yazarın tasarımını mı yoksa okurun kendi beklentilerini mi ortaya koyduğu sorusuna dayanır. Henüz bir uzlaşı oluşmamıştır ve her okuma, romanın kendisi kadar yorumcusu hakkında da bilgi verme eğilimindedir.
